surprises.head: The Rangers’ power play feasted on the Islanders’ kill
surprises.body: The Islanders have one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: the Rangers’ power play created 25.3 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.8 (about 8.6 against the Islanders) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 700 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: A hat trick for Lafrenière, and the hats come down
paras: Cole Beaudoin played his first NHL game. The Islanders’ Semyon Varlamov was back in an NHL net for the first time since Nov 29, 2024. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored his first goal for the Rangers early in the first to open the scoring. Brayden Schenn and J.T. Miller squared off midway through the period. The second period was a wild one. Alexis Lafrenière made it 2-0 for the Rangers just 25 seconds into the period. Bo Horvat and Calum Ritchie scored just under two minutes apart early in the period to tie it 2-2, but the Isles didn’t score again. Bjorkstrand scored again on the power play late in the period to put the Rangers back ahead 3-2. Lafrenière then scored into the empty net twice in the last two minutes, and it finished 5-2. Bjorkstrand and Adam Pelech fought in the final minutes. For Pelech, it was his first fight since October 2023. Lafrenière finished with a hat trick.

The Rangers had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Islanders 24-19. Igor Shesterkin made 17 saves for the Rangers. The Rangers moved to 4-1-0, still first in the NHL in points, while the Islanders dropped to 1-2-0, slipping to sixth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Rangers.
Alexis Lafrenière scored his first three goals of the season, his first since Apr 8.
The Islanders were without Mathew Barzal. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Ducks were missing more at the time.
Eeli Tolvanen’s goal streak ended at three games.
